'''Julian Washburn''' (born December 18, 1991) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Austin Spurs]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He attended and played [[college basketball]] for the [[UTEP Miners men's basketball|University of Texas El Paso]].

==High school career==
Washburn attended [[Duncanville High School]] where he saw action at point guard, shooting guard and small forward throughout his prep career. As a senior, he averaged 16 points, seven rebounds and three assists, and was rated the no. 24 small forward in the country, a top-150 player overall and a three-star recruit by Rivals.com while he was rated the no. 6 prospect in the state in the Class of 2010 by Texashoops.com.<ref name="bio">{{cite web|title=UTEP bio|url=http://www.utepathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/julian_washburn_754807.html|accessdate=October 23, 2015|work=UTEPAthletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170306035150/http://www.utepathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/julian_washburn_754807.html|archive-date=March 6, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==College career==
After graduating high school, Washburn attended the [[University of Texas at El Paso]], where he averaged 11.7 points, 3.8 rebounds and 2.1 assists in 34.2 minutes over 130 career games, finishing first in school history in total minutes (4,448), fourth in field goals (592) and sixth in scoring (1,526 points).<ref name="Wilco">{{cite web|first=J. R.|last=Wilco|title=Julian Washburn signs with Spurs|url=http://www.poundingtherock.com/2015/10/22/9600494/julian-washburn-signs-with-spurs|accessdate=October 23, 2015|work=PoundingTheRock.com|date=October 22, 2015}}</ref> On his four years with the [[UTEP Miners basketball|Miners]], he distinguished himself for his defensive prowess, being able to defend four positions on the floor and earned three All-Defensive team mentions and winning [[Conference USA men's basketball tournament|Conference USA]]'s Defensive Player of the Year Award as a senior.<ref name="bio" /><ref>{{cite web|title=2015 Conference Men's Basketball awards|url=http://csnbbs.com/printthread.php?tid=730090|accessdate=October 23, 2015|work=csnbbs.com}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Austin Spurs (2015–2016)===
After going undrafted in the [[2015 NBA draft]], Washburn joined the [[Golden State Warriors]] for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Warriors Announce 2015 NBA Summer League Roster and TV Schedule|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-announce-2015-nba-summer-league-roster-and-tv-schedule|accessdate=October 23, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=July 2, 2015}}</ref> On October 22, 2015, he signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]],<ref name="Wilco" /><ref>{{cite web|title=Spurs sign Julian Washburn|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=18492|accessdate=October 23, 2015|work=InsideHoops.com|date=October 22, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Spurs sign former Conference USA Defensive Player of the Year|url=http://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/spurs/article/Spurs-sign-former-UTEP-forward-Julian-Washburn-6585143.php|accessdate=October 23, 2015|work=MySanAntonio.com|date=October 22, 2015}}</ref> but was waived just two days later.<ref>{{cite web|title=SPURS WAIVE WILLIAMS AND WASHBURN|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-waive-williams-and-washburn|accessdate=October 24, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2015}}</ref> On October 30, he was acquired by the [[Austin Spurs]] of the [[NBA Development League]] as an affiliate player of San Antonio.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://austin.dleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-announce-2015-returning-players-and-training-camp-invitees/|title=AUSTIN SPURS ANNOUNCE 2015 RETURNING PLAYERS AND TRAINING CAMP INVITEES|date=October 30, 2015|work=NBA.com|accessdate=October 30, 2015|archive-date=November 9, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151109023821/http://austin.dleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-announce-2015-returning-players-and-training-camp-invitees/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Tigers Tübingen (2016–2017)===
After joining the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] and the [[San Antonio Spurs]] for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]],<ref>{{cite web|first=Alex|last=Nicolas|url=http://www.minerrush.com/2016/6/28/12054344/vince-hunter-julian-washburn-land-on-los-angeles-clippers-summer|title=Vince Hunter, Julian Washburn land on Los Angeles Clippers Summer League Roster|date=June 28, 2016|work=MinerRush.com|publisher=SB-Nation|accessdate=September 11, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-announce-2016-las-vegas-summer-league-roster/|title=SPURS ANNOUNCE 2016 LAS VEGAS SUMMER LEAGUE ROSTER|work=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2016|accessdate=January 3, 2017}}</ref> Washburn signed with [[Tigers Tübingen]] of the German [[Basketball Bundesliga]] on August 5, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/208818/tubingen-walter-tigers-land-julian-washburn.html|title=Tubingen Walter-Tigers land Julian Washburn|date=August 5, 2016|work=Sportando.com|accessdate=September 11, 2016}}</ref>

===Second stint at Austin Spurs (2017–2018)===
On November 2, 2017, Washburn was included in the 2017–18 opening night roster for [[Austin Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Opening Night Roster|url=https://twitter.com/austin_spurs/status/926220077795561472|website=Twitter.com|accessdate=November 2, 2017|date=November 2, 2017}}</ref> In April 2018, he helped Austin win the [[List of NBA G League champions|NBA G League championship]].

===Canterbury Rams (2018)===
On April 17, 2018, Washburn signed with the [[Canterbury Rams]] for the [[2018 New Zealand NBL season]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Egan|first=Brendon|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/basketball/103166644/canterbury-rams-add-third-american-import-completing-nbl-squad|title=Canterbury Rams add third American import, completing NBL squad|work=Stuff.co.nz|date=April 17, 2018|accessdate=April 17, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://rams.org.nz/canterbury-rams-add-julian-washburn-to-complete-2018-roster/|title=CANTERBURY RAMS ADD JULIAN WASHBURN TO COMPLETE 2018 ROSTER|work=Rams.org.nz|date=April 18, 2018|accessdate=April 18, 2018}}</ref>

===Third stint at Austin Spurs (2018–2019)===
On September 18, 2018, Washburn signed an Exhibit 10 deal with the [[San Antonio Spurs]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/spurs-julian-washburn-receives-exhibit-10-deal-from-spurs/|title=Spurs' Julian Washburn: Receives Exhibit 10 deal from Spurs|date=September 18, 2018|work=cbssports.com|accessdate=September 18, 2018}}</ref> but was waived three days later.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/spurs-julian-washburn-waived-by-san-antonio/|title=Spurs' Julian Washburn: Waived by San Antonio|date=September 21, 2018|work=cbssports.com|accessdate=September 21, 2018}}</ref> On October 22, 2018, Washburn was included in the training camp roster of the [[Austin Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://austin.gleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-announce-2018-training-camp-roster/|title=Austin Spurs Announce 2018 Training Camp Roster|work=NBA.com|date=October 22, 2018|accessdate=October 22, 2018|archive-date=October 23, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181023120939/https://austin.gleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-announce-2018-training-camp-roster/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Memphis Grizzlies (2019)===
On January 15, 2019, Washburn signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], a deal that saw him split his time between the Grizzlies and the [[Memphis Hustle]] of the [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Julian Washburn to two-way contract|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-julian-washburn-to-two-way-contract-190115|date=January 15, 2019|website=NBA.com|accessdate=January 15, 2019}}</ref> On April 10 he scored a career high 8 points against the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/201904100MEM.html|title=Golden State Warriors at Memphis Grizzlies Box Score, April 10, 2019|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en|access-date=2019-04-12}}</ref>

===Delaware Blue Coats (2019–2020)===
On July 7, 2019, Washburn was traded to the [[Golden State Warriors]] in exchange for [[Andre Iguodala]] and a protected first-round draft pick. The Warriors also received a [[traded player exception]] in the deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-trade-iguodala-20190707|title=Warriors Trade Andre Iguodala To Memphis|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2019}}</ref> He was waived on July 17, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=Warriors waive forward Julian Washburn|url=https://twitter.com/WarriorsPR/status/1151569979352834048|website=Warriors PR on Twitter|accessdate=July 17, 2019|date=July 17, 2019}}</ref>

He was named to the training camp roster of the [[Delaware Blue Coats]], which acquired his returning players rights from the Austin Spurs.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Naso |first1=Josh |title=Blue Coats acquire rights to Julian Washburn from Austin Spurs |url=https://sixerswire.usatoday.com/2019/09/04/blue-coats-acquire-rights-to-julian-washburn-from-austin-spurs/ |accessdate=December 5, 2019 |work=Sixers Wire |date=September 4, 2019}}</ref> Washburn averaged 6.5 points and 4.8 rebounds per game.<ref name="dorados" />

===Dorados de Chihuahua (2020)===
On November 3, 2020, Washburn signed with the [[Dorados de Chihuahua (LNBP)|Dorados de Chihuahua]] of the [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto Profesional]].<ref name="dorados">{{cite news |title=Dorados de Chihuahua ink DJ Cooper and Julian Washburn |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/dorados-de-chihuahua-ink-dj-cooper-and-julian-washburn/ |website=Sportando |accessdate=November 3, 2020 |date=November 3, 2020|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref>

===Return to Delaware (2021)===
On January 14, 2021, Washburn re-signed with the [[Delaware Blue Coats]]<ref>{{cite news |title=Blue Coats Announce 2021 Roster |url=https://bluecoats.gleague.nba.com/news/blue-coats-announce-2021-roster/ |accessdate=June 11, 2021 |work=NBA.com |date=January 14, 2021}}</ref> where he averaged 7.9 points, 2.6 rebounds and 1.4 assists on 42 and 36 per cent shooting from field goal and three-point range, respectively.<ref name="FraserValley">{{cite news |title=Fraser Valley Bandits Sign Former NBA, Memphis Grizzlies Forward Julian Washburn For 2021 CEBL Season |url=https://www.cebl.ca/fraser-valley-bandits-sign-former-nba-memphis-grizzlies-forward-julian-washburn |accessdate=June 11, 2021 |work=CEBL.com |date=June 11, 2021}}</ref>

===London Lions (2021–2022)===
On June 11, 2021, Washburn signed with the [[Fraser Valley Bandits]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]],<ref name="FraserValley" /> but didn't play for them. On July 9, he signed with the [[London Lions (basketball)|London Lions]] of the [[British Basketball League]] (BBL).<ref>{{cite news|first=Alessandro|last=Maggi|title=London Lions sign Julian Washburn for upcoming season|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/london-lions-sign-julian-washburn-for-upcoming-season/|website=Sportando.basketball|date=July 9, 2021|access-date=July 9, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=London Lions sign Julian Washburn for upcoming season|url=https://www.thelondonlions.com/news/403/|website=TheLondonLions.com|date=July 9, 2021|access-date=July 9, 2021|archive-date=July 9, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210709091826/https://thelondonlions.com/news/403/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Fourth stint at Austin (2023–2024)===
On November 20, 2023, Washburn joined the [[Austin Spurs]] of the [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Austin Spurs Acquire Julian Washburn|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/austin-spurs-acquire-julian-washburn/n-6033083|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=November 20, 2023|access-date=November 21, 2023}}</ref> However, he was waived on November 4, 2024.<ref>{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Austin Spurs Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Austin-Spurs/9/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=November 5, 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Washburn is the son of former NBA player [[Chris Washburn]] and Michelle Williams Washburn. He has four brothers and majored in Multidisciplinary Studies.<ref name="bio" /> His brother, Chris Washburn Jr.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chris Washburn - Men's Basketball - TCU Athletics|url=https://gofrogs.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=435|accessdate=October 9, 2017|website=gofrogs.com}}</ref> also played professionally overseas.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chris Washburn (ex Iskra Svit) signs at Kagoshima|url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Japan/news/594194/Chris-Washburn-(ex-Iskra-Svit)-signs-at-Kagoshima|date=August 27, 2019|website=asia-basket.com|accessdate=August 27, 2019}}</ref>
